styles.name: The Summiteer
styles.line: You see the top and you go. Fast decisions, straight talk, results.
strengths: Takes the lead when nobody else will
moves: A clear goal with a finish line
Freedom to do it your own way
Winning â€” and being seen to win
styles.pressure: You get impatient and blunt, and you may push people instead of leading them. Slow down one notch: ask one question before you decide.
talk: Get to the point in the first minute: what it is, what it pays, what it never promises.
Show the one-page plan and the calculator, not the whole library.
Let them decide. Ask: what would you like to do next? Then stop talking.
coach: Give them a target and a date, then step back.
Review results, not effort. Short calls.
Let them run their own line; check the line balance rule with them, because they will build one tall tower.
avoid: Telling them what to do in detail
Vague answers â€” they hear weakness
styles.sell: You sell with confidence and pace, and people follow it. Watch the two things you skip: listening, and the disclosure line. Say it every time: most members earn no commission at all.
styles.first30: Set your Fuji date on day one. Then find two lines, not one, before you try to go deep.
styles.message: Short and direct: one sentence on what it is, one number, one question. â€œHere is the plan on one page. 0.50% a day is the engine's average result, nothing is promised. Want to look at it tonight or Thursday?â€

styles.name: The Storyteller
styles.line: You climb with a crowd. Warmth, energy, stories that make people say yes.
strengths: Makes people feel welcome in a minute
Turns a plan into a story
Brings energy to a flat room
moves: People who like you and tell you so
New faces, new places, new starts
styles.pressure: You talk more and finish less, and you may promise more than the plan allows. Write the next step down, and keep every number inside the disclosure.
talk: Start with them: who they are, what they want, who they know.
Show the cartoon, not the guide. Tell the story of one member's first 30 days.
Make the next step social: a Zoom with you and one other person, this week.
coach: Praise in public, often and specifically.
Help them track: a list of names, a date next to each. They will not do it alone.
Pair them with a Mapmaker for the numbers and the paperwork.
avoid: Leaving them alone for a week â€” they drift
styles.sell: You sell with warmth and people buy you first. Watch the promises: every figure is an average, and you must say so out loud. The Language Card is your friend.
styles.first30: Name twenty people on day one. Talk to three a day, with the cartoon. Let your sponsor do the first Zooms with you.
styles.message: Warm, personal, with a picture: â€œI thought of you when I watched this four-minute cartoon. It is a software purchase, not a deposit, and nothing is promised â€” but I think you will like how it works. Coffee this week?â€

styles.name: The Anchor
styles.line: You keep the rope team together. Patience, loyalty, calm when it counts.
moves: A team you can count on
Time to get used to things
Being appreciated quietly, not on stage
styles.pressure: You go quiet and give in, and you may say yes to keep the peace. Say what you need. A calm no is still kind.
talk: Slow down. No pressure, no countdown, no 'tonight only'.
Let them read the Key Facts in their own time, and come back with questions.
Show who is already in â€” a steady person trusts a steady group.
coach: Make the plan a routine: same day, same hour, three names a week.
Reassure often; change one thing at a time.
Give them the customer documents to hand out â€” they are the best at the quiet, honest conversation.
styles.sell: You sell by trust, slowly, and your members stay. Watch the asking: you wait too long to ask for the next step. Ask for a small one, with a date.
styles.first30: One conversation a day, no more, with the Key Facts in hand. Build your first two lines from people who already trust you.
styles.message: Gentle and patient: â€œNo hurry on this. Here are the Key Facts â€” two pages, honest about the risks. Read them when you have a quiet moment, and tell me what you think next week.â€

styles.name: The Mapmaker
styles.line: You check the route before you climb. Facts, questions, careful steps.
strengths: Reads the rules and understands them
Spots the mistake before it happens
moves: Knowing how things work, all the way down
Order, accuracy, a plan that holds
styles.pressure: You overthink, delay and withdraw, and you may never feel ready. Decide with what you have; the plan is written down and you can re-read it.
talk: Give them the Momentum Plan Guide and the Breakage Differential document, and leave.
Answer every question with the rule and the page it is on. Never round up.
Show the Math Audit and the disclosure; they trust what has been checked.
coach: Respect their questions; find the answer in the documents, together.
Give them time; set a decision date, not a push.
Let them run the numbers for the team â€” and teach the Storytellers the Language Card.
styles.sell: You sell with proof and people trust it. Watch the detail: a prospect does not need every rule in the first talk. One page, three facts, one question.
styles.first30: Learn the plan cold: the guide, the line balance rule, the differential. Then teach it to one person a week; teaching is where you shine.
styles.message: Precise and sourced: â€œHere is the Momentum Plan Guide, 12 pages. The rank table is on page 3; the daily caps on page 7. Every figure is an illustration at the engine's average result, not a promise. Shall we go through your questions on Thursday?â€

blends.DI: With the Storyteller close behind, you lead out loud: fast, warm, persuasive. Watch the promises â€” keep every number inside the disclosure.
blends.DS: With the Anchor close behind, you drive hard but stay loyal: people follow you because you keep your word. Watch the impatience with slow starters.
blends.DC: With the Mapmaker close behind, you decide fast and check the route first: a rare mix. Watch the tone â€” facts said bluntly still sting.
blends.ID: With the Summiteer close behind, you are the energy and the push: great at opening, good at closing. Write the next step down before you leave the room.
blends.IS: With the Anchor close behind, you are warm and patient: people trust you quickly and stay. Watch the asking â€” you wait too long to ask for the next step.
blends.IC: With the Mapmaker close behind, you tell the story and you know the rules: the best teacher in the room. Watch the time â€” not every talk needs every fact.
blends.SD: With the Summiteer close behind, you are calm with a backbone: steady, and firm when it matters. Say the firm thing sooner.
blends.SI: With the Storyteller close behind, you are kind and sociable: the friend everyone phones first. Keep a list, or the names slip away.
blends.SC: With the Mapmaker close behind, you are careful and dependable: your members get the honest, complete answer. Decide with what you have; you will never feel fully ready.
blends.CD: With the Summiteer close behind, you are precise and decisive: you check the route, then you go. Give others the same time you give yourself.
blends.CI: With the Storyteller close behind, you explain things so people enjoy learning them. Let the story carry the fact; do not bury it.
blends.CS: With the Anchor close behind, you are thorough and patient: the one who reads the fine print for the whole team. Ask for the next step; it is not pushy, it is kind.
